headline: US stocks ended mixed as cooler July CPI eased Fed rate concerns and AI-focused technology shares outperformed
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 (SPY) closed higher, the Nasdaq (QQQ) gained, and the Dow (DIA) edged lower after July CPI showed headline inflation up 0.1% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year, slightly below the prior 3.5%.
- Core CPI rose 0.2% on the month and 2.5% year-over-year, keeping market-implied odds of a Fed hold in September near 55–60%.
- CoreWeave (CRWV) jumped after Q2 revenue more than doubled year-over-year, management highlighted an operating-leverage inflection, and the company raised its 2026 guidance.
- Super Micro Computer (SMCI) advanced on an earnings beat, strong forward guidance, and commentary pointing to sustained AI-related demand.
- Nebius Group (NBIS) rallied as AI cloud revenue increased 514% year-over-year to $575 million, reinforcing strength across the AI infrastructure complex.
- CAVA Group (CAVA) gained after reporting 9% comparable-sales growth and an earnings beat.
- Wendy’s (WEN) rose on news of activist investor interest in the company.
- Sector-wise, technology outperformed while consumer cyclicals lagged modestly on the day.
- After-hours trading saw no major earnings surprises or outsized moves beyond continued strength in AI-related names.
- Investors turned attention to upcoming inflation releases and the next slate of corporate earnings for further direction on growth and policy.
